# Reference 01 — FICTIONAL US 2019/0123456 A1, "Sealant-resistant valve core with removable insert"

**Publication number: FICTIONAL — this reference does not exist and is provided only to exercise the prior-art charting prompts.**

Applicant (fictional): Northbridge Cycle Components. Published (fictional): 25 April 2019. Filed (fictional): 18 October 2017.

## Summary of disclosure

The reference addresses the same problem as the present matter: latex tyre sealant drawn into a Presta valve core during inflation, drying on the seat and poppet, and causing leak or blockage.

The core (paragraphs [0012]–[0028] and Figs. 1–3) has a brass body with a bore enlarged to 2.8 mm to reduce capillary rise of sealant along the poppet stem. The poppet (element 24) carries a conical sealing face coated with a fluoropolymer layer (element 26) of 10–25 μm, described as reducing adhesion of cured latex. The seat (element 30) is a rigid brass shoulder machined in the body.

A removable insert (element 40, Figs. 4–5, paragraphs [0030]–[0041]) is the principal feature: a sleeve press-fitted into the lower bore that captures sealant deposits and can be pulled out and cleaned or replaced without removing the entire core. The insert is described as brass or "a rigid polymer such as acetal".

Paragraph [0036] states that the insert "may be provided with a slight flare at its lower edge to encourage sealant to drain back into the tyre when the valve is closed". Figure 5 shows this flare.

## What is absent or ambiguous (reviewer's note for testing)

- No deformable or compliant seat; the seat is rigid brass throughout.
- No over-travel of the poppet, no secondary spring stage, and no secondary flow path opened by inflation pressure.
- No mention of shape-memory or superelastic materials anywhere.
- No wiping action; the fluoropolymer coating reduces adhesion but does not remove a formed film.
- Paragraph [0022] says the enlarged bore "allows the inflation air stream to carry loose sealant back into the tyre" — this is ambiguous as to whether any purge effect is intended, and should be charted as ambiguous rather than explicit.
- Claim 1 (fictional) recites: a valve core comprising a body, a poppet with a low-adhesion coated sealing face, a rigid seat, and a removable insert in the bore below the seat.
